public_rationale: He says Cursor, Perplexity, Harvey, Lovable and Replit each burn $4 or $5 for every $1 of revenue. The cited items give gross margins only, not total spending or cash burn. At a 30 April 2026 event, Replit's CEO said reporting suggested Cursor had negative 23% margins, which implies a cost of revenue of about 1.23 times revenue. He gave no period for that figure (e1). He also said Replit had been gross margin positive for over a year (e1). In October 2025 he said Replit was gross margin positive, with 80% to 90% margins on enterprise deals (e2). These figures make 4 to 5 times total spend look doubtful for Cursor and Replit. But gross margin leaves out operating costs, so it cannot confirm or rule out the claimed ratio. No item gives any figures for Perplexity, Harvey or Lovable. With no matching revenue and total-spend data for any of the five companies, the claim is unresolved.
limitations: Gross margin is a different measure from total spending per dollar of revenue.
The margin figures are unaudited CEO statements, and the Cursor figure is his account of other reporting.
No citable spending or burn figures were found for any of the five companies; a Cursor burn figure was behind a paywall.
He gave no source or period for the ratio.

'These are all' applies the ratio to each of the five companies, not as an average.
Present tense with no period named: I use the latest period public figures could describe before the post, 2025 through Q1 2026.
Gross margin alone does not settle total spend per dollar, but it constrains it.
criteria.support_condition: Reliable figures for each named company (or most of them) showing total spending or cash burn of about 4 to 5 times revenue in 2025 to early 2026.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reliable figures for one or more named companies showing total spending far below 4 to 5 times revenue, e.g. near break-even or modest losses relative to revenue, in 2025 to early 2026.
